title: Streaming graceful-shutdown, token idempotency and reconnect workflow to prevent partial-token exposures
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Summary: On 2025-02-16 we observed a capacity scaling event that led to multiple customer sessions receiving truncated streaming responses (partial tokens) and abrupt disconnects. Root-cause signals pointed to aggressive autoscaler preemption combined with immediate worker termination without flushing in-flight KV cache and no server-client resume protocol. Several production apps reported degraded UX and increased error rates for chat endpoints during the window. Immediate mitigations included temporarily raising minimum pool size, enabling longer drain windows on the autoscaler, and adding a server-side fallback that returns a final non-streaming completion when a stream cannot be continued.
postmortem_summary: What happened: During a rapid workload spike, autoscaler reclaimed GPU workers aggressively while they were producing streaming tokens. Without a graceful shutdown path, workers were terminated mid-emit and clients received partial tokens or socket disconnects. Why it happened: (1) runtime shutdown path did not guarantee KV cache flush and final token emission; (2) streaming protocol lacked sequence numbers or resume tokens to allow clients to request continuation; (3) SDKs lacked resume semantics and retry logic for half-completed chunks; (4) observability did not surface partial-token metrics or per-stream continuation failures. Impact: multiple customers saw garbled assistant messages, a spike in error-rate/latency for streaming endpoints, and a few support tickets escalated to SEs. Permanent fix plan below.
action_items: ENG: Implement server-initiated graceful shutdown hook in runtime (owner: Daniel Park) — ensure final buffer flush, KV cache draining, and explicit stream-close with a resume token if continuation is possible. Target: runtime-1.20. Estimate: 5.

ENG: Add sequence-numbered token chunks and idempotency metadata on stream frames (owner: Marina Soto) — frame format v2 with seq/offset to detect duplicates and reassemble partial tokens. Estimate: 3.

SDK: Add client resume and dedupe logic across SDKs (JS / Python) (owner: Priya Nair) — auto-resume when a valid resume token present, expose opt-in config for strict vs best-effort resume. Estimate: 3.

Infra: Change autoscaler policy to prefer safe drain over immediate preemption for streaming-tier jobs (owner: Kevin Liu) — min-drain 45s for streaming pools, with configurable emergency override. Estimate: 2.
QA: Create e2e tests simulating mid-stream preemption and verify resume behavior and non-duplication of tokens (owner: Sofia Alvarez) — integrate into CI gating. Estimate: 3.
Observability: Add metric 'stream.partial_tokens' and a per-stream 'resume_attempts' histogram; dashboard and alert when partial_tokens > 0.5% of streams for 5m (owner: Jamal Roberts). Estimate: 2.
Docs/SDK: Document resume semantics, failure modes, and recommended retry backoffs for customers (owner: Emily Chen). Estimate: 2.

Rollout: Canary server runtime release to 5% of streaming traffic, monitor partial_tokens, connection_drop_rate, and user-visible message truncation; proceed to 50%/100% with FD (owner: Daniel Park). Estimate: 2.
Follow-up: Run a small customer beta with 3 large chat customers that experienced the incident to validate UX before full rollout (owner: Solutions Eng - Alex Romero). Estimate: 1.
Post-deploy retrospective: 2-week metrics review and a retro meeting to confirm no regression and adjust drain configs if needed (owner: Aisha Malik). Estimate: 1.
